title: How to rotate ssh keys safely
overview: Rotating SSH keys regularly reduces the blast radius of a leaked credential. [1] Good key hygiene means never reusing a single SSH key across unrelated systems. [2] Rotate keys at least once a year, and immediately after any suspected compromise. [2]

key_findings.text: Rotating SSH keys regularly reduces the blast radius of a leaked credential.
Good key hygiene means never reusing a single SSH key across unrelated systems.

children.text: Verify you can authenticate with the new key, then remove the old public key from authorized_keys on each host.

key_findings.text: Rotate keys at least once a year, and immediately after any suspected compromise.
First generate a new key pair with a strong algorithm such as ed25519.
Store private keys encrypted with a passphrase and prefer a hardware token where possible.
Add the new public key to every server the old key could access before removing anything.

sections.heading: Key facts
sections.body_md:
- Keep an inventory of which keys authorize which hosts so rotation never locks you out. [2]
- Finally revoke the old private key from any agent and delete it. [1]
